title: Information content versus word length in random typing
venue: Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment 2011(12):L12002 (arXiv:1209.1751)

cost.compute_notes: arXiv PDF (8 pp) read in full. Closed form checked by simulating 200,000 words of generalized random typing (reanalysis/rt1_check.py); about a minute.

triggers: is the linear relation between information content and word length evidence of optimization
random typing baseline for language efficiency claims
Piantadosi word length information content critique
monkey typing produces Zipf's law of abbreviation

claims.statement: For a generalized random typing process (unequal character probabilities, minimum word length l0), the expected information content of words of length l is exactly linear, I0(l) = a*l + b with a = (H(S) + p0 ln p0)/(1 - p0) and b = ln((1 - p0)^l0 / p0); with word-level context I(l) = I0(l). Hence a linear information-length relation does not by itself indicate any optimization (contra Piantadosi et al. 2011).
claims.scope: Analytic; context defined by neighbouring words (or characters with l0 = 0). Does not test whether real texts' slopes and intercepts match random typing.

quantities.name: random_typing_information_length_linearity_r2
quantities.unit: R2 of OLS of simulated mean -ln p(w) on word length l = 1..8
quantities.source: reanalysis/rt1_check.py (27 symbols, p0 = 0.18, Zipf-like letter probabilities, l0 = 1)
quantities.baseline: simulated means match the closed form a*l + b (a = 3.032, b = 1.516) within 0.016 nats at every length

our_assessment.why: Derivation read in full and checked by simulation: exact up to sampling noise. This is the prior art for the structural-null argument recorded in maria2026-structural-null-semantic-efficiency, in a different object (word length, not category partitions): a process with no pressure toward efficiency reproduces the signature read as efficiency. The authors themselves mark the open part: whether real texts' slope and intercept match random typing's.

open_questions: Do real texts' I(l) slopes and intercepts match random typing with the same character statistics? The authors leave it open; corpora with letter-level statistics would answer it cheaply.
Moscoso del Prado 2013 (CogSci, 'The missing baselines...') remains unread in full -- download blocked 2026-10-16.
